summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of morbid obesity, psoriatic arthritis, obstructive sleep apnea, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and exertional chest pain following a recent hospitalization for edema. Initial workup ruled out cardiac ischemia, pulmonary embolism, and heart failure. Echocardiogram was suboptimal, but cardiac MRI and stress testing showed normal left and right ventricular function with no evidence of ischemia. Bi-atrial enlargement and mild pulmonary artery dilation were noted, but symptoms were determined to be non-cardiac. Pulmonary consultation suggested a restrictive ventilatory defect due to obesity. The patient's edema improved with furosemide, gabapentin was dose-reduced, and new respiratory symptoms were managed with inhaled bronchodilators. Diarrhea developed during admission and responded to Donnatol. He was discharged home on optimized medical therapy with plans for outpatient pulmonary follow-up and weight management.
